newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU aid office honours media with awards.
newsitem.headline: EU aid office honours media with awards.

text.p: A Swedish documentary about the Liberian civil war won the Forgotten Conflict prize at the first European Community Humanitarian Office (ECHO) television and radio awards on Monday.
The documentary, directed by Anders Ribbsjo of Sveriges Television, was among six awards handed out to the media to honour its role in informing the world about humanitarian crises.
They were made public at a ceremony in Dublin attended by Irish President Mary Robinson, a champion of developing world rights, and Emma Bonino, European Commissioner for Humanitarian Affairs.
Senegalese musician Youssou N'Dour and British Broadcasting Corporation reporter Martin Bell were among the panel of judges which studied 220 entries from all 15 EU member states.

Bonino said the awards provided "an opportunity to acknowlege the vitally important role that the broadcast media has played in making the public aware of the extent of human misery throughout the world.

"Whether the stories tell of individuals of conflicts, past or present, forgotten or otherwise, the ECHO awards acknowlege the role and the power of the media in reminding the public of the cost of human suffering."
L'Aube (Dawn) directed by Danis Tanovic, Belgium
In the minds of the People:
Enemy my Friend, Micke Finlason, Eydeas, Britain
The Dead are alive; Rwanda, an eyewitness, Director Anna Van der Wee, Wild Heart Productions, Belgium
The plight of Turkish writers, Reporter Ali Erginsoy, Producer Tim Whewell, Eurofile, BBC Radio 4, Britain
The Hague Diaries, Coverage of U.N. War Crimes Tribunal, Internews Team, Europe.
ECHO is an EU Commission service under Bonino's responsibility charged with managing humanitarian aid to all non-EU countries.
